title: SD SDIO and eMMC overview: establish mode and voltage
summary: Select the device type, supported bus width, I/O voltage and operating mode. Review clock, command and data requirements before routing.
applies_to: Initial SD/MMC interface review; exact host and peripheral documentation governs.
required_inputs: Host/peripheral versions, mode, I/O rails and initialization requirements
verification: Compare power states, pull configuration and timing at both ends.
limitations: SD memory, SDIO peripherals and eMMC are not interchangeable; this overview is not an HS200/HS400 specification.

title: Removable SD card and SDIO routing review
summary: Review CMD/data pulls, clock integrity and card-detect behavior. Include connector loading and external protection in the channel review.
applies_to: Removable SD or board-level SDIO links; peripheral-specific signals vary.
required_inputs: Connector or peripheral pinout; host pull and voltage requirements
verification: Inspect CMD/CLK waveforms and initialization; verify card detection where present.
limitations: OMAP44xx resistor and ramp-time examples must not become universal rules. SDIO devices may need additional enable or interrupt signals.

routing: Review signal loading, clock ringing and protection capacitance.
return_path: Maintain a continuous reference through connector escape.
pitfalls: Do not apply one pull-up value to every host and mode.

title: eMMC power and bring-up review
summary: Review power and I/O validity, boot configuration and CMD/data behavior before attributing failures to routing. Capture waveforms and check host configuration.
applies_to: Initial eMMC bring-up; cited OMAP44xx troubleshooting is device-scoped.
required_inputs: Host and memory requirements, rails, boot state and target mode
verification: Verify initialization, read/write integrity and supported speed transitions.
limitations: Detailed HS200/HS400 strobe routing is not covered. Obtain the selected SoC and memory design guides before setting high-speed geometry.
